chunk-001:c003.proposition: Explanatory intuitions applicable to ordinary contingent objects need not extend to material reality as a whole, whose ultimate existence may instead be brute.

orphanFallback.rationale: Clifton independently limits ordinary explanatory intuitions at the level of all material reality, thereby constructively supporting brute ultimate reality without requiring an earlier opposing move.

chunk-001:c005.proposition: Even if the universe is contingent and has a first temporal moment, its existence may be brute because causal intuitions formed within time need not govern time's ultimate boundary.

orphanFallback.rationale: The source directly distinguishes a first moment from coming into existence within time and uses that distinction to advance a standalone case for brute cosmic existence.

chunk-001:c007.proposition: Calling a foundation necessarily existent does not explain why it exists, because the attributed necessity applies only conditional upon that foundation's existence.

orphanFallback.rationale: Clifton's source-grounded distinction between existence and the conditional property of necessary existence independently challenges necessity's claimed explanatory value.

chunk-001:c010.proposition: Divine supremacy cannot noncircularly explain necessary existence if necessary existence is itself among the greatness-making properties that constitute divine supremacy.

orphanFallback.rationale: The source identifies reciprocal explanatory dependence between supremacy and necessity and independently asks what fact makes the alleged necessity obtain.

chunk-002:c002-05.proposition: Failure to exist in every possible world need not imply dependence, because an ultimate being could be independent while existing in only some possible worlds.

orphanFallback.rationale: Clifton expressly separates world-relative nonexistence from causal dependence, supplying a standalone modal distinction that permits an independent but contingent foundation.

chunk-002:c002-07.proposition: Logical laws may regulate language, statements, and inference without constituting a mind-independent ontological structure capable of grounding concrete reality.

orphanFallback.rationale: The source independently disputes that logical rules exist as an ontological landscape, directly weakening any constructive bridge from logical necessity to a concrete foundation.

chunk-002:c002-09.proposition: The necessity of mathematical propositions has an intelligible basis in the incoherence of their denial, while no analogous fact has been shown to make a concrete God incapable of nonexistence.

orphanFallback.rationale: Clifton independently contrasts an intelligible basis for mathematical necessity with the missing basis for concrete divine necessity, establishing the abstract-to-concrete gap.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-02.proposition: A foundational reality may simply be brute, and no inference from its lack of a further explanation to its existence in every possible world has been established.

orphanFallback.rationale: The source grants a foundation while independently rejecting the leap from foundational bruteness to modal necessity, directly limiting what foundational inference can establish.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-04.proposition: Necessary existence does not explain why God exists, and any acceptable brute-foundation status available to God appears equally available to the universe.

orphanFallback.rationale: Clifton directly argues both that necessity adds no understanding and that brute foundational status applies equally to God and the universe, forming a standalone parity objection.
